document.title: [Feature]: Candidate-only scoring for DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer consumers on SM90 (H20)
document.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

> **Scope:** this is a CUDA / SM90 (Hopper) request. ROCm is referenced only as prior art — the bot CC'd ROCm maintainers on keywords, apologies for the noise.

DeepSeek-V4.1's two-level indexer publishes candidate blocks at `candidate_source_layer_id`; later consumer indexers are meant to select their top-k **inside those candidate blocks only**. On SM100 this is implemented with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels (`fp8_fp4_(paged_)sparse_mqa_logits`). On SM90 there is no equivalent, so the consumers fall back to dense scoring over the full context followed by a mask.

vLLM currently implements candidate-consuming indexers in one of two ways:

1. **SM100** — `fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits` / `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` via `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`. Opt-in through `AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits` and hard-gated on SM100-class hardware (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py`, the `is_device_capability_family(100)` check), the MXFP4 indexer cache, DeepGEMM >= 2.8, and the DeepSelect extension.
2. **ROCm (gfx950)** — candidate-only MQA scorers reading the candidate pool in place, in review as #57858 (prefill) and #57859 (decode).
3. **SM90 (H20)** — neither. The consumers run the full-width `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py` and then mask the scores down to the candidate blocks with `_apply_candidate_mask` (`vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py`). The candidate mechanism keeps the semantics but not the compute saving.

Measured on H20 (SM90), TP8, 1M context, decode, FP8 indexer cache, torch profiler:

| Concurrency | Per consumer layer | 4 consumer layers | Share of a step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ~10 | 2.067 ms | 8.28 ms | 20% of 40.75 ms |
| 1 | 196 µs | 0.78 ms | 6% |

Layers 24/28/32/36 each make one full-context `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` call per step. With `candidate_topk_blocks` = 2048 and `candidate_block_size` = 8, the candidate set is 16 384 positions against a 1 048 576-position compressed context — **1.6% of the scored columns** — so roughly 98% of each consumer's scoring work is discarded by the mask. The cost scales linearly with both concurrency and context length.

The requested feature is a CUDA/SM90 way to score only the candidate blocks.

### The MXFP4 coupling blocks SM90 today

`indexer_sparse_logits` cannot be enabled on SM90 at all, and not only because of the GPU-family check. The flag also requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`sparse_indexer.py`, and again in `models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`), and MXFP4 itself is rejected before that:

```python
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py
if use_fp4 and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
    raise ValueError(
        "indexer_kv_dtype='mxfp4' requires Blackwell datacenter GPUs "
        "(sm_10x, e.g. B200/GB200); sm_120 (consumer Blackwell) and "
        "earlier architectures are not supported."
    )
```

Hopper has no FP4 datapath, so SM90 necessarily runs the FP8 indexer cache (the `auto` default, one float32 scale per token). MXFP4 is an input requirement of the SM100 DeepGEMM kernels, not part of the "score only the candidate blocks" semantics — the ROCm path, for instance, scores the candidate pool with fp32 logits. So enabling candidate-only scoring on SM90 means letting that semantic flag be satisfied by an FP8 implementation.

**Question for maintainers:** should candidate-only scoring on SM90 reuse `indexer_sparse_logits` (relaxing its MXFP4 requirement to a per-platform one), or should it be a separate opt-in with its own builder type? The former keeps one user-facing knob and makes a future SM100 migration a no-op; the latter keeps each platform's preconditions self-contained.

### Alternatives

- **A. Gather + reuse the existing dense kernel (preferred).** Consumers gather their candidate K from the index cache (~2 MB per request) and score the gathered candidate set with the existing dense logits kernel, dropping the mask pass. No new scoring kernel. The scored K set and the query are identical to the dense-then-mask path, so the resulting logits should be bit-identical. A relevant primitive already exists on CUDA: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (`torch.ops._C_cache_ops`, added in #25931 / #26456) gathers paged indexer K — FP8 values plus the 4-byte scale — into a contiguous workspace, and the prefill path uses it today. It gathers contiguous ranges addressed by `cu_seq_lens`, so it is a starting point rather than a drop-in: candidate-block gathering needs scattered block IDs.
- **B. Native SM90 sparse MQA-logits kernel.** Mirrors the SM100 DeepGEMM semantics with a new SM90 kernel, removing the gather hop. Better ceiling, substantially more implementation and validation cost.
- **C. Two-level selection inside the consumer (HISA-style).** Block-level coarse pass plus a refined pass inside the candidates. Extends the saving to the candidate-source layer and the ratio-2 layers, but changes the scoring semantics and needs accuracy re-validation. Better treated as a follow-up.

Both A and B need a profitability gate, because gathering loads more per key than the dense walk. #57858 measured the crossover at ~1.0–1.5× `span/capacity` and gates at 2.0×. This workload sits at 62.5×, well above the gate, so the gate should not engage in the target scenario.

### Additional context

**Relationship to existing work.** This is the SM90/CUDA counterpart of the ROCm candidate-only scorers. #57858 (prefill) and #57859 (decode, open) implement candidate-only scoring on gfx950, with measured operator speedups of 3.28× (66 rows, ctx 72.1k) and 4.85× (192 rows, ctx 88.5k), and +5.80% end-to-end output throughput with −4.9% p90 TPOT at TP=4, C=32. They list the same consumer layer positions (24/28/32/36). Those PRs are ROCm-only and touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`; the CUDA path is unimplemented. This is not a duplicate of them, though all three would touch `candidate_blocks.py`, so ordering matters.

Related, and deliberately out of scope here:

- #56254 wired the DeepGEMM sparse MQA-logits kernels into the V4.1 indexer. Its stated scope is SM100-class GPUs, and it documents "there is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path". That is the scoring path this issue proposes to extend to SM90, not to replace.
- #59204 (draft, conflicting) enables the DeepSelect sparse-indexer **top-k** on sm90. That covers the selection stage, not the scoring stage, and does not touch the SM100 gate on the sparse-logits backend.
- #61039 (merged 2026-10-14) made candidate selection length-aware in the decode indexer, removing ~850 µs/step of full-width work at 1M. It explicitly keeps the full-width path as the fallback when DeepSelect is unavailable, so **SM90 does not benefit from it**: `has_deep_select()` is SM100-only, so `select_candidate_blocks` keeps `FULL_WIDTH=True` on Hopper and still runs `torch.topk(2048)` over the full width. SM90 does have usable top-k backends (`cooperative`, `persistent`), so the same length-awareness looks portable. That is a separate, much smaller item (2.1% of a step at conc≈10, but ~6.5% at conc≈1) and would most naturally ride along with the scoring work rather than be filed on its own.
- The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash kernels tracker (#56217) has no discussion of non-SM100 hardware.

**Open items to validate.**

1. Candidate block alignment: `candidate_block_size` = 8 vs the kernel page sizes (32/64).
2. Bit-identical results between the gather path and the current dense-then-mask path, to be confirmed by measurement rather than assumed.
3. The profitability threshold tuned for SM90 rather than copied from the ROCm measurements.
4. Whether the FP8 indexer record (`head_dim` + one float32 scale) gathers efficiently into the layout the dense kernel expects on SM90, where `mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` is False.

**Environment (target).**

```text
GPU: H20 (SM90, Hopper)
TP: 8
Context: 1M
Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
Indexer K cache: FP8 (MXFP4 is unavailable on SM90, see above)
```

**Status.** Happy to implement the SM90 candidate-only scoring path (alternative A), but the flag question above decides where the code lands, so filing this first to get direction. The measurements above predate #61039; they will be re-taken on current main before any PR.
